fields.statement: At dd9192ca I built the branch binary and the merge-base ebee728a binary outside PATH. I cloned this repo (1746 log entries) to a scratch dir, set rhiza.daemon.paused=true, selfUpdate=false, minFree=0 and an eventCommand, and ran each binary's real `rhiza daemon --permission-mode auto` in the foreground. I read the process's utime+stime from /proc over a 60 s idle window after a 20 s warm-up. Base binary: 5912 ticks, about 59 CPU-s in 60 s (~98% of a core), which reproduces the fault. Branch binary: 108 ticks, about 1.1 CPU-s in 60 s (~2%). Its first fold took about 3.5 CPU-s and later polls stayed at about 1-2 ticks/s. `rhiza daemon status` showed Last poll advancing, Paused: yes, and the full Skipped list, so the picks and skips were still worked out every poll from the cached fold. The VM load average was 8-20 on 4 cores.

At dd9192ca, with the branch binary's real `rhiza daemon` running paused on a scratch clone of this repo, I sampled its CPU every 5 s while changing things from another process. `git branch qa-scratch-ref` (a ref move) cost 361 ticks in the next window, which is one re-fold, and then it went back to idle. `rhiza daemon set rhiza.daemon.maxRuns 3` (a setting) cost 346 ticks, then idle. `rhiza change new` (a log entry) caused re-folds over the next polls, then idle. `rhiza propose` caused re-folds, and the event command ran exactly once, writing one line {"event":"proposed","change":"01M6HF4SM0QW..."}. No moves already in the log were replayed. Before each change the daemon sat at idle CPU, so the cached fold was in use. I did not exercise daemon start/resume invalidation hands-on, because that would launch real agents. The daemon logs had no errors.
